name: SHT30 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Sensirion SHT30-DIS digital temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.2 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±2 % typical) sensor with an I2C interface. Runs on 2.15–5.5 V with 10 kΩ pull-ups on SDA/SCL. Sold as: DFRobot Fermion: SHT30 Digital Temperature & Humidity Sensor (SEN0330; 6-pin header VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, INT, RST), I2C address 0x45 as shipped (ADDR pulled high; cut-jumper J1 for 0x44).
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.15–5.5 V (use your board's 3.3 V so the I2C pull-ups match its logic level)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Alert output (chip ALERT pin, active high), not needed for basic use

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Reset, active low (internal pull-up in the chip); leave unconnected for basic use

supplierQuery: DFRobot SEN0330 Fermion SHT30 temperature humidity sensor
buildNotes: This board answers at I2C address 0x45 (ADDR is pulled up through 1 MΩ); bridging/changing jumper J1 ties ADDR to GND for 0x44. Many clone SHT30 modules use 0x44 instead: run i2c.scan() if unsure.
Single-shot command 0x24 0x00 then wait at least 15.5 ms before reading 6 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC, humidity MSB, LSB, CRC.
Check each CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
Power VCC from 3.3 V: the on-board 10 kΩ pull-ups go to VCC, so 5 V on VCC would put 5 V on the ESP32/Pico SDA and SCL pins.
Leave INT and RST unconnected for basic use; RST is pulled high inside the chip.
Keep the sensor away from the board's regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air around them.

driver.code:
# SHT30 temperature & humidity sensor (Sensirion SHT3x-DIS), MicroPython driver.
# Single-shot, high-repeatability measurement without clock stretching (command 0x2400),
# CRC-8 checked as in the datasheet (poly 0x31, init 0xFF).
# DFRobot Fermion SHT30 (SEN0330) ships with ADDR pulled high: address 0x45.
# Boards with ADDR low (most clone modules) use 0x44.
import time


def _crc8(data):
    crc = 0xFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x31) & 0xFF if crc & 0x80 else (crc << 1) & 0xFF
    return crc


class SHT30:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x45):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def read(self):
        """Measure once and return (temperature in °C, relative humidity in %)."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x24\x00')
        time.sleep_ms(20)  # high repeatability takes up to 15.5 ms
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 6)
        if _crc8(d[0:2]) != d[2] or _crc8(d[3:5]) != d[5]:
            raise OSError('SHT30 CRC mismatch: check the wiring')
        t_raw = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        h_raw = (d[3] << 8) | d[4]
        return -45 + 175 * t_raw / 65535, 100 * h_raw / 65535

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def humidity(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def soft_reset(self):
        """Soft reset (command 0x30A2); the sensor is ready again after 1.5 ms."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x30\xa2')
        time.sleep_ms(2)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sht30 import SHT30

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = SHT30(i2c)  # 0x45 on the DFRobot board
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
